editorial.marketOverview: Friday's holiday-shortened rally remains the latest cash session. Nasdaq rose 2.31%, SOX approximately 4.7%, and Barchart reports Nasdaq 100 up 2.61%. WSJ reports broad sector participation and a 6.7% weekly Nasdaq rebound after a 10% weekly decline. Low holiday volume reduces confidence in extrapolation.
editorial.whatChanged: The repository score improved marginally from -13 to -12 at 22:05 ET, with unchanged positive breadth and chip leadership. Open Watch timestamp remains November 28 02:31 UTC and no new dated curated catalyst was found. Fresh calendar reporting identifies Marvell and Credo calls on Tuesday evening, adding a clearer Wednesday semiconductor catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The rebound is consistent with relief rather than confirmed trend reversal. Repository yields remain 4.936% and 4.710%, implying 22.6 basis points without rescaling. WSJ reports December tightening remains widely expected. Reuters confirms Brent 95.44 and WTI 83.08 settlements and expects unchanged OPEC+ targets, but supply risks persist. No live weekend price response is available.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday tests the rally under normal liquidity following Sunday's OPEC+ meeting; Rubrik reports after close. Tuesday's ISM and JOLTS at 10 ET may shift yields, followed by Marvell and Credo calls at 16:30 and 17:00 ET. Wednesday ADP at 08:15 ET and the response to chip guidance could determine whether leadership persists; Salesforce and Snowflake report after close, so their main cash reaction may fall outside the horizon.
editorial.bullCase: Broad participation and sustained semiconductor relative strength, combined with easing volatility and stable or lower yields, could extend Friday's rebound. Constructive chip guidance would reinforce the demand narrative.
editorial.bearCase: A reversal in chip leadership, renewed oil supply disruption or yields above 5% could unwind the relief rally. Weak AI infrastructure guidance or hotter macro data could intensify valuation pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor OPEC+ outcome, Sunday futures reopening, Monday breadth and fresh paired yields and volatility. Compare Tuesday macro releases with expectations and distinguish earnings guidance from observed Wednesday market response.
